# Answer-engine citation log (GEO)

Each SEO/GEO cycle puts a rotating handful of real buyer questions to an answer engine and
records whether oxfordagentic.com appears, and what is cited instead. Rotate the questions;
do not re-run the same set every cycle. Engine: Perplexity search (ranked sources), unless
noted. These are snapshots, not rankings: results vary by engine, location and day.

## 2026-11-27 (08:00 UTC cycle) - THREE PROBES, ZERO CITATIONS, THE FORTY-FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SET - AND ALL THREE DECLINE, WITH THE CYCLE'S CHANGE COMING FROM A GUARD RATHER THAN FROM A FIELD

**Engine: web search, not Perplexity** (no Perplexity route from the sandbox since 12 Oct), US-resident, so
the 26 Oct caveat about reading positions off this instrument stands. **Production could not be read**:
`oxfordagentic.com` is refused at CONNECT by this sandbox's egress proxy (HTTP 403) and does not resolve
through `WebFetch` either; `luma.com` is refused the same way. No live page was read, no Luma fact was
checked, no event fact was touched, deploy state came from the Actions API, and every site fact below comes
from committed files or built output. The outbound link check is the third instrument saying the same thing:
**0 of 12 third-party links reachable**, including both Luma pages, so every one of those warnings is this
sandbox rather than a broken link.

**Dedupe by backlog 136's method, tenth use.** Question strings extracted and counted before any search ran.
**Dropped as already worked**: hire-versus-train (`hire someone` 4, `recruit` 6, and the build-versus-hire
axis is on the record), hackathons (`hackathon` 8), away days (`away day` 15), webinars (`webinar` 13),
duration framings (`enough` 7, `one day enough` 3), slides-versus-hands-on (`slides` 10, `lecture` 6).
**Dropped as banned or unanswerable**: the location and travel axis (permanent), certification, step-free
access. The three taken score 0 to 3.

| # | Question | oxfordagentic.com cited? | What answered instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | will an AI agent workflow I build today still work after the model is updated in six months maintenance (durability / model-churn axis - `obsolete` 1, `fragile` 0, `keep working` 0) | **No** | mindstudio.ai x3, learn.microsoft.com x2, dev.to, gravitee.io, pydantic.dev x3, ai.pydantic.dev, rkalani1.github.io, opusresearch.net, tianpan.co, community.latenode.com, blog.promptlayer.com |
| 2 | how do I teach the rest of my team what I learned at an AI training day cascade the learning (cascade / internal-teaching axis - `teach the rest` 0, `teach my team` 0, `train the trainer` 0, `cascade` 2) | **No** | trainingmag.com x2, culturalsynergies.com x2, td.org, learningwiki.unitar.org x3, britishcouncil.org, mcc.gov, pluralsight.com, scaledagileframework.com, asana.com, heller.brandeis.edu, rhythmsystems.com |
| 3 | is a lunch and learn session enough for AI skills or do you need a full day workshop for a business team (format-intensity axis, lunch-and-learn arm - `lunch and learn` 0) | **No** | mentorcruise.com x6, lilachbullock.com x2, insivia.com, atlassian.com x2, learning.sap.com, brainstation.io, d3.harvard.edu, fanshawec.ca, sites.google.com |

**Reading, probe by probe.**

- **Probe 1 passes winnability on the letter and fails on who is asking, which is the gate that catches
  good-looking topics.** The field is vendor engineering blogs (`mindstudio.ai` three times) and platform
  documentation (`learn.microsoft.com`, two `pydantic.dev` changelogs, `gravitee.io`), and the engine's
  answer is about golden test sets, pinned model versions, semantic versioning of workflow components and
  deprecation watch. **That searcher is an engineer keeping agents alive in production, not a leader
  deciding whether to spend a day in a room.** Traffic from it is the "AI bootcamp vs course" failure the
  12 August rule was written about. Microsoft is also in the field on its own product, which is the other
  half of the same rule.
  - **The honest residue, recorded and not acted on.** There is a leader-shaped version of this objection -
    *does the thing I build in a day still earn its keep in six months* - and this site does not answer it
    in those words. But it is not this field's question, and answering it would need a claim about how our
    own attendees' workflows have held up, which is an outcome fact nobody here has. **Do not re-open the
    durability axis as an engineering page.** If it is ever re-opened it is as the leader's objection, and
    it needs evidence from past cohorts first.

- **Probe 2 declines on winnability in the cleanest form the rule describes: institutional publishers on
  their own subject.** Cascade training is a named L&D method with a literature, and the field is that
  literature - the **British Council**'s train-the-trainers cascade toolkit, three pages of **UNITAR**'s
  learning wiki, **ATD** (`td.org`), `trainingmag.com` twice, a **US government** lessons-learned page, the
  **SAFe** framework, Brandeis. The engine answered confidently with a figure from that literature (*"the
  target audience gets only 75% of the original content"*). A provider page does not outrank that and
  should not.
  - **The reframe the rule asks for, and why it stops at an ask rather than a page.** What that field never
    answers is the AI-specific version: what exactly can one attendee hand a colleague after a hands-on
    day. For us that runs straight into **backlog 146** - the Coding line publishes a take-home kit and the
    Agentic line's four published outcomes contain nothing a colleague could read - and into **backlog 147**
    on who helps afterwards. So this is the second consecutive day on which a cascade-shaped question
    resolves to the same unanswered product fact, which is dated evidence for 146 rather than a topic.

- **Probe 3 is winnable and converting and was still declined, on the ground the engine itself named.** The
  field is vendor marketing - `mentorcruise.com` six times, which is one host's duplicated template rather
  than six sources - with institutional publishers present but not dominant (`learning.sap.com`,
  `d3.harvard.edu`, `fanshawec.ca`). The searcher is splitting a budget between a free internal session and
  a paid day, which converts. **But the engine closed with "the vendor sources have commercial reasons to
  recommend longer, paid formats", and a tenth vendor page arguing that a full day beats a lunch hour is
  exactly that.** The conference arm shipped six hours ago on the opposite basis: it could name when a
  conference is the better buy. Here the honest answer - a lunch-and-learn is a fine taster and a poor
  build session - is both true and indistinguishable from self-interest, and the duration question is
  already answered on the programme page.
  - **Recorded as the second format arm of `ai-bootcamp-vs-course-vs-exec-education`, deliberately unspent.**
    Two arms of one guide in one day would also breach the loop's own one-refresh-per-cycle rule. If it is
    ever taken, it needs a reason a reader would believe from someone who sells the longer format - most
    likely a published account of what a lunch hour actually gets through, which is an outcome fact we do
    not hold.

**What the cycle shipped instead, and why it is in this log.** The three probes produced no copy, and the
change came from the guard that protects the claims this log keeps measuring: `check-dates.mjs` would have
let `/guides/when-ai-executive-cohorts-run/` publish *"The days still on sale are a fourth agentic day on
3 December"* on 4 December with a green build, because its `OURS` gate holds `cohort` and `bootcamp` and
that clause says "agentic day". That page is where a buyer asking when the next day runs lands, and the
21 November probe in this log is an engine doing exactly that and being sent to a passed cohort's booking
page. The full measurement is in the Shipped entry in `IMPROVEMENTS.md`.

## 2026-11-27 (02:00 UTC cycle) - THREE PROBES, ZERO CITATIONS, THE FORTY-THIRD CONSECUTIVE SET - AND ONE OF THE THREE CONVERTS INTO A SHIPPED SECTION RATHER THAN A BACKLOG ITEM

**Engine: web search, not Perplexity** (no Perplexity route from the sandbox since 12 Oct), US-resident, so
the 26 Oct caveat about reading positions off this instrument stands. **Production could not be read**:
`oxfordagentic.com` is refused at CONNECT by this sandbox's egress proxy (HTTP 403) and does not resolve
through `WebFetch` either, and `luma.com` is refused the same way. No live page was read, no Luma fact was
checked, no event fact was touched, deploy state came from the Actions API, and every site fact below comes
from committed files or built output.

**Dedupe by backlog 136's method, ninth use.** 710 question strings extracted and counted before any search
ran. **Dropped as already worked**: worth-it framings (`worth` 35), group and team buying (`group` 16,
`colleague` 5), sector cuts (`sector` 16), non-technical fit (`non-technical` 13), free material (`free` 8),
substitution framings (`instead of` 10). **Dropped as unanswerable or banned**: tax and expense treatment
(`tax` 0, `expense` 0), because VAT treatment is a standing decision never to state and "can I expense it"
is advice this site cannot give - recorded so no later cycle mistakes a zero count for an opportunity. The
three taken score 0 to 2 on the question list.

| # | Question | oxfordagentic.com cited? | What answered instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | is a one-day hands-on AI workshop better value than an AI conference ticket for a business leader (format-comparison axis, conference arm - `conference` 2) | **No** | acceleratetomorrow.com, thesmallbusinessexpo.com, codebridge.tech, ventionteams.com, primeconcepts.com, poppymarketingandconsulting.com, womeninaiglobalsummit.com, ritwikjoshi.com, brainiacconsulting.io |
| 2 | what happens when you get stuck after an AI training workshop who do you ask for help afterwards (post-day-support axis - `stuck` 0, `afterwards` 3, `support` 6) | **No** | propellernet.co.uk, teamland.com, trivana.ai, futurefactors.ai, blueshore.ai, aimadethisbrand.com, authentilead.co, amivo.co.uk, aiedgeconsult.com |
| 3 | do you need to know how to code to build an AI agent in a one day course no coding required (coding-prerequisite axis - `python` 1, `beginner` 2) | **No** | udemy.com x2, classcentral.com, youngurbanproject.com, aitoolssme.com, agentman.ai, onedayagent.company, completeaitraining.com, theaischool.co, courses.impodays.com |

**Reading, probe by probe.**

- **Probe 1 is the cycle's change, and it is the first probe in six weeks to convert into shipped copy
  rather than a backlog item.** Nine results, every one a vendor, a conference promoter or a consultancy,
  and **no institutional publisher anywhere in the field** - the engine flagged its own field unprompted
  (*"Most of the sources are vendor marketing pages, so treat their claims as positioning"*). Winnable.
  Converting: the searcher is allocating a training budget between two line items. **What made it
  actionable rather than merely winnable is that the gap is on our own page**:
  `ai-bootcamp-vs-course-vs-exec-education` compares executive education, an online course, a bootcamp and
  doing it free, and says nothing about a conference, which is the other line in most AI training budgets.
  Acted on this cycle - a `## Where a conference fits` section with two leaf `h3` questions, which took
  that guide's `FAQPage` node from 3 Questions to 5.
  - **The second phrasing is the reason the section is written the way it is, and it is worth recording
    as a method note.** Asked the short way - *"AI conference or AI training workshop which should I send
    my team to"* - the field collapses into "best AI conferences 2026" listicles (`splunk.com` three
    times, `datacamp.com` five, `bizzabo.com`, `startupstash.com`, `uvik.net`, `getmaxim.ai`) and the
    engine answered with US conferences (GTC, Databricks, ODSC) rather than with the decision at all.
    **Two phrasings of one axis, two completely different fields**: the comparison phrasing holds the
    decision and is winnable, the short phrasing is a listicle farm and is neither winnable nor
    converting. The section is written for the first and does not chase the second.
  - **Why this is not a second vendor arguing its own corner**, which is the failure mode the engine named
    in its own field. The section gives conferences real credit and names when a conference is the better
    buy - the same move as *"When is a paid day not worth it?"* already on that page. A comparison that
    cannot say when not to buy from us is positioning, and the field is already full of it.

- **Probe 2 is a reach failure, not a coverage gap, and the distinction was checked rather than assumed.**
  The engine declined a general answer - *"The search didn't turn up a universal answer, since
  post-workshop support depends on the provider"* - and closed by telling the reader to *"ask the organizer
  or trainer"*. The field is nine vendor pages advertising 30 days of email support, 60-minute check-ins at
  2 to 4 weeks, and optional monthly calls. **We publish an answer to this question already**: *"What
  happens after the day?"* on the Agentic programme page and in the homepage FAQ, both inside `FAQPage`
  nodes, so it is machine-readable and simply was not reached.
  - **One honest asymmetry, measured and not acted on.** The field's question is *who helps me when I am
    stuck*; our published answer is about what you leave with and the group you leave with - *"you go away
    with their contact details, and people stay in touch afterwards"*. Those are different questions, and
    the second does not answer the first. Whether Oxford Agentic offers anything resembling the field's
    30-day email support is **a product fact only Drummond holds**, and writing one would be inventing a
    term of sale. **Filed as backlog 147.** That makes three consecutive days on which the binding
    constraint was a product fact rather than a field (145, 146, now 147), which is itself the finding
    worth reporting.

- **Probe 3 declines on the field being saturated with exactly the claim we would make, which is a
  different decline from the usual one and worth naming.** Ten results, all vendor or course marketing,
  no institutional publisher - so it passes the letter of winnability. It fails in substance: nine of the
  ten already say "no coding required" about an online no-code course, and the engine answered the
  question confidently and correctly without us. Publishing a tenth page saying "no coding" wins nothing.
  - **The one real distinction in that field, recorded and deliberately not written up.** "No coding" there
    means drag-and-drop builders - Langflow, n8n, a vendor's own agent builder - whereas our days mean
    plain-language instruction to an agent that writes the code itself. That is a genuine difference, but
    the message house rule is that "no coding" is never left standing on its own, and the site already
    draws the distinction in `agentic-ai-glossary` (*"the constraint is clear thinking about your task, not
    code"*) and on the Coding Bootcamp page. **No action. Do not re-open the coding-prerequisite axis as a
    "no coding" page**; if it is ever re-opened, it is as the drag-and-drop-versus-coding-agent distinction
    and nothing else.

**Reading, probe by probe.**

- **Probe 3 declines on winnability in the clearest form this log has recorded, and it should not be
  re-probed.** Seventeen results and fourteen are law firms or professional publishers writing on their own
  subject - Sprintlaw **seven** times, plus Khurana & Khurana, BCL, Aaron Hall and the British Library. That
  is the institutional-publisher half of the gate, exactly. It fails converting too, and in a way worth

  book, and the honest answer to their question is "read your employment contract", which no provider page
  can give them. **No action. Do not re-open the IP-ownership axis.**

- **Probe 1 is a real gap in the field and this site cannot honestly fill it today.** The engine declined
  outright - *"The search didn't turn up a standard UK booking cutoff for one-day AI courses. Each provider
  sets its own rules in its terms and conditions, and the pages I found mostly link to those terms rather
  than stating the deadline"* - and what it found instead is each provider's own store page: NTU twice, LSBU
  three times, QA three times, plus CII, City Lit, Salford, Global Knowledge and Flane. It did surface two
  specifics that read as the field's real behaviour: CII says a booking *"will only be confirmed once payment
  has been processed"*, and that a workshop may be postponed *"subject to a minimum number of bookings"*.
  - **Winnable**: yes, and unusually so. Every page in that field is a provider selling its own course, not a
    publisher owning the question. No institutional publisher holds it.
  - **Converting**: the strongest intent this log has seen. Someone asking how late they can book is trying
    to book. **Cohort 4 is seven days out as this is written**, which is precisely the week this searcher
    exists.
  - **Why nothing shipped anyway, and it is the same shape as backlog 145 from this morning.** The answer is
    a fact only Drummond holds. Luma closes bookings, not this site, and Luma is unreachable from this
    sandbox, so the loop cannot even read when the current cohorts' sales close. What the site does publish
    is adjacent and does not answer it: the transfer assurance, "no refunds", and payment by invoice. Writing
    "book up to the day before" or "bookings close at midnight" would be inventing an event fact, which is a
    hard guardrail. **Filed as backlog 146, with the sentence he would need to supply and the three places it
    would go.**

- **Probe 2 is the same answer arriving from a different direction, plus one measured asymmetry.** The engine
  declined again - *"The search didn't turn up a general answer, since it depends on the specific workshop"* -
  and its field is weaker than probe 1's: four Google Docs exports, a GitHub gist, a Stanford teaching-commons
  DIY kit and two vendors' own workshop pages. That is half winnable at best, and converting only moderately,
  because someone asking what they keep is comparing rather than booking.
  - **The asymmetry is real and was measured rather than assumed.** `/bootcamps/agentic-coding-bootcamp/`
    publishes *"A take-home kit of the prompts and commands used on the day"* in its outcomes. The Agentic
    programme's four `outcomes` are the pipeline, the pattern, the judgement line and the room - all true, and
    **not one of them is a thing you can read after the day**. Grepped across the whole Agentic programme file:
    no mention of prompts kept, slides, notes or materials.
  - **No change, for the same reason as probe 1.** Whether an Agentic attendee leaves with anything written is
    a product fact. The Coding line's answer cannot be copied across, because the two days build different
    things. **Folded into backlog 146 as its second half rather than filed separately**, since one answer from
    Drummond settles both and they would be written in the same cycle.

**No new guide, and none is warranted on this evidence.** Three probes, three declines, and the two that
decline on a missing fact rather than a lost field are now one backlog item with the question written out.

figure, which is the right answer and already shipped. Re-probe only if follow-up data ever exists; that is the

### Probe 4 - the question one of our own guides is named after - NOT CITED, AND IT SEPARATES REACH FROM RELEVANCE MORE CLEANLY THAN ANY PROBE IN THIS LOG

returned. **That is reach, and nothing written on this domain changes it.** It is the ninth consecutive
measurement pointing at backlog 2b.

**The competitive half is new and is a positioning reading rather than an SEO one.** Of the sixteen results,
**twelve are developer or machine-learning bootcamps**: `codecademy.com` twice, `coursera.org`,

bootcamp" means a multi-week developer course**, and the task it expects you to bring is a training dataset.

has behaved differently from every query that did not. **Recorded as an observation for Drummond, not as a
change**: nothing was rewritten on the strength of one probe, and a title or positioning move on this axis is
his call, not the loop's. Filed as backlog 134.

**No new guide.** Four probes, four declines - one because the page already exists, two on the winnability rule,
one on accuracy. Thirty-two guides, newest `publishDate` 20 October, none published this week.

  all three tests, and the reasons are worth recording because this admission will recur.

    sector specialist: `events.icaew.com` returned five dated in-person classroom sessions of
    *Generative AI for accountants*, and `astranti.com` five pages of one-day AI training sold
    separately to law and to accountancy. An institutional publisher writing its own CPD
    calendar and a competitor with a sector-specific one-day format are exactly the two
    categories the rule excludes.

    *tailored to a small firm*. This site's format is deliberately the opposite - one real task
    per person, cross-sector, facilitated rather than taught to a syllabus - so the honest answer
    to that query is that we do not do the thing being asked for. Writing a page that implies
    otherwise would assert a tailoring the site does not offer.

    `agentic-ai-for-public-sector-and-nhs-leaders` already hold the sector axis. A fourth is the
    near-duplicate query variation rule 6 bars, and professional services is the closest of the
    four to the three already published.
- **Probe 2 is a demand signal rather than a content one, and it is the first of its kind in this
  log.** Every other declined probe has been declined because the site already answers the question
  or cannot win the field. This one is declined because **the field is answering a question we have
  decided not to answer**: the aggregators returned evening courses (Forth Valley, 12 sessions of
  7pm to 9pm), live-online half-days (Reed, a four-hour instructor-led Copilot course) and
  term-time part-time formats, against our single 09:00 to 17:00 day. There is no page to write -
  the answer is "a full day, in person" and that is already published on every surface - but the
  volume of evening and half-day supply on a buyer-phrased query is a format observation for
  Drummond, not a gap in copy. **Recorded as backlog 107, not acted on**: the loop does not invent
  a format.
- **Probes 1 and 3 are declined on the standing rule and need no new argument.** Probe 1's field is
  ten vendor and consultancy blogs writing about their own product category, which fails WINNABLE
  outright, and `agentic-ai-glossary` plus `what-is-an-agentic-bootcamp` already make the
  distinction the engine spent its answer making. Probe 3's field is law firms and compliance
  consultancies plus three `.pages.dev` microsites; it fails CONVERTING, because someone checking
  whether the AI Act reaches them is doing due diligence rather than looking for a day in Oxford,
  and `getting-an-ai-workflow-past-it-and-legal` already carries the adjacent argument.
- **Zero citations across four questions. Reach, not coverage, for the twenty-fifth consecutive
  cycle.** Nothing in these four results is a coverage gap: one is already written twice, one is a
  question we answer and the engine did not reach, one does not convert, and one asks for something
  the format deliberately is not.

| do I need a written down process before I automate a task with an AI agent | **No** | `help.webex.com` (x2, one article), `trupeer.ai` (x3, the same page in French, Chinese and Polish), `consultevo.com` (x2) |

**Reading.**

- **Probe 3 is the finding, and it is the thinnest field recorded here.** Seven results for a
  question a buyer plausibly types the week before booking, and the whole field is one vendor
  help article about configuring its own agent builder, one page served three times in three
  languages, and one consultancy post. Not one institutional publisher. **Winnable.** And
  **converting**: whoever types it is working out what they have to do before they can automate
  anything, which is the moment before booking a day whose premise is "bring one real task from
  your own work". The engine's own hedges are the quality gap: ***"no law or platform requires a
  formal written process"*** and ***"Most of the advice comes from automation consultancies and
  vendors, so treat it as practitioner opinion rather than settled standards"***.
- **And the site does not answer it.** `how-to-choose-your-first-agentic-task` publishes five
  tests for picking a task - you do it repeatedly, it runs on words and documents, you can check
  the output at a glance, it is annoying enough to care about, getting it wrong is affordable -
  and **not one of them is "can you write the steps down"**. Nothing in the 65 published FAQ
  questions asks it either. So this is a content gap rather than a discovery problem, which is
  the opposite of what 1, 2 and 3 November found.
- **It was not written this cycle, deliberately, and the reason is a ceiling rather than a
  doubt.** The right home is the Agentic programme page's FAQ block, because that is a page
  engines reach and the guide is not - the 4 August decision keeps guides unlinked from
  commercial pages, and the August Search Console baseline says the guide class is not being
  crawled. **Two FAQ entries have already shipped today**, at 02:00 and at 08:00, which is the
  stated daily ceiling for that class of change. Recorded as **backlog 64** with the probe
  attached, so the next cycle can take it without re-deriving the evidence.
- **Probe 4 is correctly a miss and must not be chased.** The engine said outright ***"I found no
  in-person, one-day agent-building course in England for December 2026"***, and the one December
  date it found is in Belgium. **We do not run a December date** - Cohort 3 is 19 November and the
  Coding Bootcamp 26 November - so being absent from a December query is the true answer, not a
  defect, and inventing a reason to appear there would mean inventing a date. What it does
  corroborate, for the eighth dated reading since 27 October, is the standing split: this query
  names England rather than Oxford, and we were not reachable. Nothing on the page fixes that
  (backlog 2b).
- **Two probes declined.** The scattered-information question is **not winnable**: Google Cloud
  and Microsoft are both in the field on their own products, which is the rule's
  platform-vendor case, and the honest answer to that searcher is the Second Brain day, where the
  standing decision is that ranking is not its constraint and demand is. The team-fear question
  is winnable and **does not convert**: the field is change-management consultancies and content
  farms, the engine answered it completely with eight pieces of advice, and whoever types it
  wants a script for a meeting rather than a day in Oxford building a workflow.

  articles"*. The second re-probe closes the same way - *"none measures a six-month window

  *"### Should I wait until the tools settle down?"* and *"### Does what I learn go out of date
  in six months?"* since August - as `h3`s, which the extractor could not see. Backlog 57, which

  field is thin and winnable - one provider's own FAQ page on a `pages.dev` host, BrainStation,
  and a scatter of individual event listings - and the engine's synthesis lands on our own
  positioning, *"the thing that makes the day worthwhile is a real task of your own"*, while
  citing other providers for it. But *"What should I bring?"* is already a hand-written `faqs`
  entry on the Cohort 3 event page and inside its `FAQPage` node, and the answer ("A laptop, and

  on-page fix. This is discovery again, which is backlog 2b.**
- **Probe 3 is the sixth dated reading of the discovery problem, and the first on the flagship,
  17 days out.** An availability-shaped query for exactly what we sell - in person, UK, agentic,

## 2026-10-26 (13:00 GMT cycle) - THE "THREE URLS" READING IS AN INSTRUMENT ARTEFACT. READ THIS BEFORE CITING IT AGAIN.

**Engine: web search, not Perplexity** (no Perplexity route from the sandbox, as on every
cycle since 12 Oct). Four rotating buyer questions, then **three probes written to test the
log's own standing diagnosis** rather than to find a topic.

| Question | oxfordagentic.com cited? | What else ranks |
|---|---|---|
| hands-on agentic AI course Oxford one day business leaders next cohort (domain-restricted) | **Yes**, forced: `/`, `after-the-ai-executive-programme`, `claude-cowork-claude-code-or-codex` | n/a, restricted to our own domain |
| AI away day for a leadership team UK one day hands-on build something in person | **No** | **innovationvisual.com six of nine** (per-city pages: Nottingham, Manchester, Birmingham, London, Edinburgh, plus custom and leaders), ivee.jobs, createwith.com (Leeds, Sept 2026) |
| agentic AI training for executive assistants and office managers UK hands-on course | **No** | cegos.com, **pitman-training-london** (one-day, GBP 479, Holborn), euromatech.com (5-day, Dubai/Paris), infosectrain.com, mediatraining.ltd.uk, esami-africa.org, emploilr.com |
| which tool should a non-developer build their first AI agent in n8n Zapier or ChatGPT | **No** | clickittech.com (x2), **mindstudio.ai (x2)**, datacamp.com (x3 locales), upwork.com, codeconductor.ai |

### The three instrument probes, and what they overturn

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `"Whose morning does the task eat"` (exact phrase, domain-restricted) - a string that exists on `/guides/who-should-take-the-seat/` and nowhere else | Returned **the same three URLs** as the unrelated buyer question above, and the engine said *"The search didn't return any direct match"* |
| `"Peer level matters more in a small room than the syllabus"` (exact phrase, domain-restricted) - a string on `questions-to-ask-before-booking-ai-training` | **The domain restriction was ignored outright.** Nine results, all USPTO patents, arxiv and NCBI. Not one from our domain |
| `cookie policy data retention privacy` (domain-restricted) | **One** URL, `/`, and the answer was quoted off the consent banner that appears on all 63 pages. `/privacy/` was not returned |

**Reading. The standing line in this log - "a domain-restricted search returns the same three
URLs whatever is asked, so the engine holds only three pages of this site" - is not a
measurement of anybody's index, and no cycle should prioritise work on the strength of it.**

- Verified first that the target string is live and indexable, so the probe was fair: the
  phrase is present in `dist/guides/who-should-take-the-seat/index.html`, that URL is in
  `sitemap-0.xml`, the page returns 200 with a correct self-canonical and no robots meta, and
  it shipped on 19 October, a week before this probe.
- An exact-phrase query is the sharpest retrieval test available from here, and it returned a
  set that **does not contain the page containing the phrase** while containing three pages
  that do not. A query-invariant result set is a property of the tool, not of a corpus.
- The second probe settles it: **the same tool, on the same cycle, ignored `allowed_domains`
  completely.** An instrument that silently drops its own filter cannot be used to enumerate
  what a domain has in an index.
- The third shows the result count is not fixed at three either - it was one - so the triple
  is not a stable "what the engine holds" set in any sense.

**What the loop actually has on index coverage, and it says something different.** The
Search Console baseline of 24 August 2026, the only real index measurement in this repo,
reads **23 indexed and 16 not indexed, 35 discovered, sitemap status Success**. Its diagnosis
was **crawl budget on a domain registered 22 July with zero external links** - "not a
technical fault, not fixable on-page" - with the measured counter-evidence that
`/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/` had **257 inbound internal links and had never been
crawled once**. So the one hard reading the loop owns is 23 pages indexed two months ago and
an off-page constraint, not three pages indexed and an on-page one.

**What this costs, concretely.** Cycles 40, 44, 45 and the structured-data cycles of 25-26
October each reasoned from the three-URL premise - "the homepage is the only page the engine
holds", "a property added to `courseSchema()` reaches the indexed page as well as the
unindexed ones", "`/events/` is not in the index to be re-read, which is why its 21 Oct fix
moved nothing". None of those changes was harmful and each is defensible on its own terms,
but the premise under them was produced by this instrument and is not supported. **Stop
inferring index coverage from a web-search tool.** The only things that can answer it are the
Search Console Pages report (backlog 2, Drummond, two minutes) and a fresh crawl reading.

**And it re-points the loop at what was always the measured constraint: external links.**
Backlog 2b was downgraded on 10 August from "binding" on the strength of *search-result*
positions read through this same class of instrument. The 24 August crawl data was never
overturned by anything, and it names one external link as the thing that moves crawl budget.
`Organization.sameAs` is still empty. That is Drummond's call and it is now the top ask.

### The four buyer questions, briefly

- **Away day: NOT WINNABLE, and not converting either. Do not re-pitch it.**
  `innovationvisual.com` holds **six of nine** results with one page per city - Nottingham,
  Manchester, Birmingham, London, Edinburgh - which is exactly the doorway pattern this site
  has a hard rule against, so the field is won by a tactic the loop will not copy. Converting
  fails independently: a leadership away day is a private team booking, and this site sells
  individual seats in a mixed cohort where you bring your own task.
- **Executive assistants and office managers: a real product gap, and still a decline on
  converting.** The engine was explicit - *"I found no UK course that specifically teaches
  agentic AI to executive assistants or office managers"* - and the field is training
  providers rather than institutional publishers, so winnable is arguably satisfied. But the
  programme's published `whoFor` is senior people who have hit the ceiling of the chat window,
  and an EA or office manager is not that buyer. Writing for a persona the day is not built
  for would be traffic we cannot convert and a promise the page does not keep. Recorded, not
  written. (Field note: Pitman's own listing shows "next date 21st October 2026" on one copy
  and 7 October 2025 on another, so stale dating is endemic here, not just on our listings.)
- **Tool choice for a non-developer: vendor and comparison blogs, and we already hold the
  ground that matters.** clickittech, mindstudio, datacamp, upwork and codeconductor take all
  nine. `claude-cowork-claude-code-or-codex` is one of the two guides this tool returns for
  our domain at all, so the site's tool-comparison position is the strongest it has, and a
  second page on n8n-versus-Zapier would compete with it while chasing searchers picking a
  free tool rather than booking a day.
- **No stale-listing reading this cycle, and one engine misreport that is NOT ours to fix.**
  The domain-restricted cohort question was answered correctly off our own homepage - *"Cohort
  3 on 19 November 2026 at Worcester College"* and the Coding Bootcamp *"on 26 November"*,

**No guide. 0 of 3 for the week of 26 Oct - 1 Nov, and the allowance is deliberately unspent

**Reading.**

- **The approval axis is a real gap and it held across three phrasings.** No page of ours
  came back on any of them. What the field offers is two things that are not the same as an
  answer: course listings with a price attached, and generic "get your boss to pay for your
  AI education" posts written for multi-week American career-change courses. The one closest
  to the question, a provider's own employer-pays template, stops at "cover what the course
  teaches, how long it takes, what it costs and who will invoice". WINNABLE by the ledger's
  test, because no institutional publisher owns it - it is blogs and vendors. CONVERTING as
  strongly as anything the log has tested: the searcher has already decided they want the
  seat and is working out how to be allowed to take it. **Written this cycle** as

- **Both engines converged on advice our format already satisfies and generic training
  cannot.** Probe 3: tie it to a priority the manager already owns, *"name concrete
  deliverables"*, and avoid vague benefits - *"swap 'I'll understand AI better' for specific
  outputs ... a pilot automation for a recurring manual task"*. Probe 5: commit to a
  measurable thing and a follow-up checkpoint, because *"training often fails without
  follow-up"*. A course that teaches a subject cannot tell a buyer what their deliverable
  will be. A day that runs against one real task the attendee brings can, and that is what
  the new guide is built on. The gap is not that the advice is missing; it is that nobody
  writing it can supply the deliverable.

  these are vendor sources with no independent ROI data."* The field's business cases run on

  a single workshop. The guide therefore tells the reader **not** to promise a number they
  have not measured, and points at the published caution that effort moved around is not
  time saved. Promising the artefact is the honest version and the one that can be checked.

**Correction to the 12 Oct 18:47 entry, now that the source has been traced.** Yesterday's
note referred to "a study of 1,237 participants" reporting expected savings far larger than
measured ones, reaching us through a Chinese tech-media summary and a LinkedIn post. Both
secondhand sources had **conflated two companion papers**, which is exactly why the rule
exists. Traced and read at the primary source:

- **arXiv:2605.23177**, *Cognitive offloading and the speedup illusion in human-AI
  interaction*, Yu, Cheng, Jabbar, Sucholutsky, Collins, Jurafsky and Hawkins, submitted
  22 May 2026, in the proceedings of the Cognitive Science Society's 48th meeting.
  Preregistered, **N = 1237**, simple cognitive tasks. Actual completion times with and
  without AI did not differ; participants predicted AI would be significantly faster; the
  bias was absent for imagined human help; subjective effort was lower with AI despite
  equivalent times.
- **arXiv:2605.22687**, *The efficiency-gain illusion*, same seven authors, 21 May 2026.
  Three preregistered studies, **N = 2691**. People frequently use AI where it saves
  neither time nor effort, and prior use entrenches the miscalibration.

The "55.7 seconds predicted versus 7.5 actual" figure circulating secondhand belongs to the
second paper's Study 2, not to the N = 1237 study, and sits in the body rather than the
abstract. **The guide shipped this cycle cites only abstract-level findings that were read
at source, and states the papers' own scope limit - simple tasks, not workflows.** Author
institutions were not listed on the arXiv pages and are therefore not claimed anywhere.

**Reading on this cycle's probes.**
- **"Bring your own real work" has stopped being a differentiator.** Ten providers answer
  that question and every one of them promises it: your own files, your own backlog, no
  demo data, small rooms, trainers walking the tables. Our nine-questions guide already says
  the descriptions have converged; this is evidence the convergence has reached the thing the
  site leans on hardest. **That is a positioning question for Drummond, not something a guide
  fixes.** What still appears rare in that field is a published agenda with named build
  blocks and an honest account of what does not fit in a day.
- Automation versus agent is owned by AWS, Zapier, Slack, Oracle, monday.com and Moveworks.
  Definitional queries belong to the platforms. The glossary sits at position 52.6 on 63
  impressions and will not move. Do not chase it.
- **theoxfordaischool.com for the third day running.** It now appears in the UK training
  comparison, the budget-justification question and the bring-your-own-work question.
